name: MA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with an 11-point partisan lean
Trahan's massive financial advantage ($1.8M cash vs ~$6K)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: Lori Trahan is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by 11 points, and her Republican opponent has raised only about $7,000. Markets price her win at roughly 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major outside spending against Trahan is the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Lori Trahan, the Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by 11 points. She faces Republican Gary Grossi, who has raised only about $7,000 and had roughly $5,800 on hand, while Trahan has raised more than $1.6 million and holds $1.8 million in cash. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but lacks visible resources. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals, fundraising, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at about 96 percent. The combination of incumbency, a favorable partisan lean, and an overwhelming money gap makes this a Safe Democratic seat with little evidence of competitive risk.
